title: Audit log SIEM + RBAC v2 + Evidence Automation - proposal
body:
Purpose:
This working proposal ties three parallel initiatives: RBAC v2 (richer role/context labels), audit-event schema harmonization for SIEM export, and an automated evidence bundling pipeline for regulatory e-discovery and forensics. The goal is to define a minimal, extensible audit event schema and a migration/versioning strategy that lets consumers (SIEMs, internal analytics, and compliance teams) evolve without breaking downstream rules.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: API gateway events, control-plane actions (deployments, rollouts, key rotation), auth decisions, admin UI actions, Dedicated/Private control-plane events. Not in scope: low-level kernel telemetry or ephemeral worker logs (those remain infra logs).
- Constraint: many SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo, Elastic) prefer flat JSON or newline-delimited JSON. We design for NDJSON export and a compact CSV fallback for ingest-limited customers.
- Backwards compatibility is a must: existing parsers rely on canonical_event and outcome fields.

Design principles:
1) Canonical event name + minimal envelope: keep canonical_event_type (dot.notation) as the primary discriminator.
2) Stable top-level fields: ts, version, canonical_event_type, principal_id, principal_type, resource_id, resource_type, outcome, request_id, rbv (rbac version token).
3) Extensible freeform meta blob: meta_kv for unstructured info (key/value strings).
4) Evidence pointers: do not embed heavy payloads in events; reference single-object evidence bundles with cryptographic integrity metadata.
5) Versioning: semantic event_version with migration rules; consumers must accept unknown fields.

Proposed top-level schema (NDJSON-friendly):
- ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp string
- event_version: schema version string (e.g. "audit.v1")
- canonical_event_type: string (e.g. "auth.token.create")
- principal_id: string (user/service id)
- principal_type: string (user|service|system|robot)
- principal_roles: array-of-strings (current RBAC labels attached at time of event)
- resource_id: string
- resource_type: string
- outcome: string (success|failure|partial|deferred)
- request_id: string (global request id)
- rbac_context: string token or short label pointing to RBAC snapshot used for decision (e.g. "rbac-v2::2024-11-01::rev-34")
- evidence_url: string (signed object store URL)
- integrity_sha256: string (sha256 of evidence bundle)
- meta_kv: stringified-kv or small map encoded as JSON string

Note: meta_kv intentionally kept as a JSON string field for SIEM compatibility in case downstream systems expect flat objects; we will provide parsing helpers in SDKs.

Example NDJSON line (literal, for format reference):
{
  "ts": "2024-11-05T18:22:31Z",
  "event_version": "audit.v1",
  "canonical_event_type": "auth.token.create",
  "principal_id": "usr_0123",
  "principal_type": "user",
  "principal_roles": ["engineer", "dedicated-operator"],
  "resource_id": "model:ggml-13b:rev3",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req_7890",
  "rbac_context": "rbac-v2::2024-11-01::rev-34",
  "evidence_url": "s3://redwood-evidence/prod/evt-abcdef12345.tar.gz",
  "integrity_sha256": "3b7f1a...",
  "meta_kv": "{\"latency_ms\":\"18\",\"route\":\"hosted-api-us-west2\"}"
}

RBAC v2 mapping notes:
- RBAC v2 introduces role labels and attribute-based assertions (org, team, environment). We will emit the snapshot label in rbac_context (compact) and principal_roles (expanded) for convenience.
- Principle of minimal authority: do not infer roles in the event consumer — emit the asserted labels at decision time.
- For decisions made by the policy engine (allow/deny), include policy_id, policy_rev in meta_kv.

SIEM export formats and consumption patterns:
- Primary export: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) persisted to an object store and optionally forwarded to SIEM via connector (S3 -> Splunk/Elastic ingest).
- Secondary export: compressed CSV flattened with canonical_event_type and a JSON-string meta column for customers that require tabular exports.
- Near-real-time stream: Kafka topic with the same NDJSON envelope. Kafka messages will set a small delivery TTL and be replayable from object-store snapshots.

Evidence automation (forensics/e-discovery):
- Evidence bundle concept: a single tar.gz that contains: raw request/response (redacted per PII policy), UI screenshots or action traces if applicable, policy decision logs, and a small manifest.json describing included filenames, sizes, and checksums.
- Storage: signed objects in dedicated evidence bucket with lifecycle and WORM mode for regulated tenants. We add server-side KMS signing and include kms_key_id in event.integrity metadata.
- Integrity model: each bundle is SHA256 hashed; optionally CMS-signed with Redwood signing key. Event.integrity_sha256 and event.integrity_signature_kms are top-level fields.
- Retention and access: evidence ACLs separate from log ACLs. Evidence retrieval must require a separate authorization flow with an audit trail.

Versioning and migration strategy:
- Semantic event_version: audit.v1, audit.v2, etc. Consumers must accept unknown fields.
- Additive changes allowed within a major version. Breaking changes increment major version.
- Migration timeline:
  * audit.v1 (current): stabilise the top-level envelope and evidence pointer semantics (target Q1 after approval).
  * audit.v2: add richer RBAC snapshots + explicit policy decision objects inline (target after RBAC v2 GA).
  * audit.v3: compressed binary event payloads for high-volume paths (experimental).
- Backcompat shim: event_transformer lambda that maps new fields to legacy fields for older consumers; deploy on ingestion path for 12 months after a major schema bump.

Rollout checklist (draft):
- [ ] Finalize field list and publish JSON schema (open draft).
- [ ] Update SDKs (python/js/go) to include serializer/deserializer helpers and evidence upload helpers.
- [ ] Implement RBAC snapshot tokenization in policy engine and emit rbac_context.
- [ ] Wire Kafka and NDJSON object-store export pipelines.
- [ ] Build transform-lambda for backward compatibility (shim).
- [ ] Create SIEM parsers / Splunk app with field extractions and macros.
- [ ] Run a 2-week pilot with one internal product team (Dedicated).

Open questions / risks:
- Evidence size limits: what is the maximum allowed per event? Proposal: 50MB default, configurable per org. Large evidence should be split into linked bundles.
- PII handling: do we redact before bundling or store encrypted and mark bundle as PII? Recommend redaction in 95% of cases; for legal hold, keep encrypted raw with limited access.
- RBAC snapshot blowup: snapshotting whole RBAC state per event is costly. We will implement compact snapshot tokens that map to stored snapshots in an internal store; events include token, not full snapshot data.
- SIEM ingestion costs: NDJSON object-store with connectors reduces SIEM ingest volumes by allowing on-demand pulls and configurable retention.

Next steps (short horizon):
1) Review with Policy Engine (Priya) and SRE (Lars) for feasibility and storage cost estimates.
2) Publish draft JSON Schema and open a GH PR for SDK changes.
3) Schedule pilot with Dedicated product for week of 2024-12-15.

Notes to reviewers: This is a working doc — expect shorthand and TODO markers. Please add comments inline in Confluence link or tag me on Slack (#sec-compliance).
